themes_detail.label: Animal Infestation Surge in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints spiked to 12 this week versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1820% increase (z-score: 16.34)—suggesting an acute wildlife or pest crisis in Bushwick's park spaces that demands immediate investigation into underlying causes and public safety risks.
evidence: 12 animal-in-park complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1820% spike, z-score 16.34)
This represents the single largest statistical anomaly in 311 data for the district
Timing coincides with street sweeping and maintenance spikes, suggesting possible environmental trigger
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department and residents at affected parks to determine what animals (rats, raccoons, coyotes) and what triggered the sudden influx
Investigate whether construction, sanitation gaps, or seasonal migration patterns are driving the spike; connect to broader rodent complaint trend (225% increase last week)

themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 112 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 16.9 per week (564% spike, z-score: 9.62), indicating potential water main breaks, pressure issues, or contamination affecting multiple buildings across Bushwick.
evidence: 112 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 16.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (564% increase, z-score 9.62)
Spike occurred 2 weeks before maintenance/facility complaints also spiked (442% increase last week), suggesting cascading infrastructure failure
Community Board has repeatedly requested green infrastructure evaluation with DEP—suggests pre-existing water system concerns
reporting_angles: Request NYC DEP emergency service logs and soil boring reports from 2 weeks ago to identify water main breaks or pressure drops
Canvass affected blocks to document outages, boil-water advisories, or low-pressure issues; identify if spike was geographically concentrated

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Dumping Spike
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 24 two weeks ago versus 6.4 weekly average (276% increase, z-score: 7.36), while illegal dumping hit 36 complaints (284% increase, z-score: 6.37), suggesting coordinated neglect or removal-service breakdown across the district.
evidence: 24 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.4 weekly average (276% spike, z-score 7.36)
36 illegal dumping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.4 weekly average (284% spike, z-score 6.37)
Both spikes occurred in same week, suggesting common cause: e.g., DSNY staffing shortage, removal service gap, or targeted vandalism campaign
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY district manager about graffiti removal contracts and resource allocation 2 weeks ago; determine if crews were reassigned or struck
Walk neighborhoods with highest concentrations to photograph and geo-map the clusters; interview residents about whether dumping increased or removal slowed

themes_detail.label: Park Maintenance and Noise Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Park maintenance complaints surged 442% (21 complaints last week vs. 3.9 baseline, z-score: 11.79) and park noise complaints jumped 700% (5 this week vs. 0.6 baseline, z-score: 6.29), suggesting Bushwick parks are becoming less safe and usable for residents.
evidence: 21 maintenance/facility complaints last week vs. 3.9 weekly average (442% increase, z-score 11.79)
5 park noise complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.29)
Converges with animal-in-park spike (12 this week) and Community Board's long-standing requests for new/expanded parks and green infrastructure
reporting_angles: Attend a community board meeting or reach out to board members to learn which parks are most affected and what maintenance items are overdue
Visit top-complaint parks (Marcy, Maria Hernandez, etc.) to assess visible deterioration, broken equipment, or late-night activity causing noise

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Service Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 6 this week versus 0.6 weekly baseline (860% spike, z-score: 7.72), paired with illegal dumping and graffiti surges, indicating possible DSNY sanitation service disruption or reallocation in Bushwick.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% increase, z-score 7.72)
Spike is most recent (this week) among sanitation signals; follows graffiti and dumping spikes from 2 weeks ago
Community Board has submitted recurring capital budget request for 'Other capital request for DSNY'—suggests long-standing service gaps
reporting_angles: Call DSNY to request current sweep schedules and ask if routes, frequency, or crew assignments changed this week
Photograph streets with multiple complaints to document debris accumulation and visible service decline
